nodes.title: Reducing Tool Hallucination via Reliability Alignment
nodes.notes: Xu et al. Relign + RelyToolBench (from StableToolBench). Four subtypes; RePR and benefit-cost utility. Indecisive actions: defer / clarify / switch tool.

nodes.title: LLM-based Agents Suffer from Hallucinations: A Survey of Taxonomy, Methods, and Directions
nodes.notes: Lin et al. First comprehensive survey of hallucinations in LLM agents. Workflow-stage taxonomy; 18 triggering causes; mitigation/detection review. Does not ship a new bench.

nodes.title: When Agents Do Not Stop: Uncovering Infinite Agentic Loops in LLM Agents
nodes.notes: Hou et al. IAL-Scan static analysis: Agent IR + ALDG. 6549 repos; 68 confirmed IALs in 47 projects (91.9% precision). Detector/eval corpus rather than a behaviour bench.

nodes.title: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use
nodes.notes: Thaman. Multi-step tool tasks; 13 models; exploit 0–13.9%; RL post-train DeepSeek-V3 0.6% vs R1-Zero 13.9%; 72% CoT-rationalized exploits. ICML 2026.

nodes.title: AgentMisalignment: Measuring the Propensity for Misaligned Behaviour in LLM-Based Agents
nodes.notes: Naik et al. Propensity (not capability) suite. More capable agents misalign more on average; persona often outweighs model identity. Multi-behaviour so pack left unknown.

nodes.title: Goal Misgeneralization in Deep Reinforcement Learning
nodes.notes: Langosco et al. ICML 2022. First empirical goal-misgen: agent keeps capabilities OOD but pursues the wrong goal. Precursor to LLM agent misspec / mesa-objective work.

nodes.title: Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity
nodes.notes: Krakovna et al. DeepMind blog (~60 examples). Blog seed: hop-1 is named works only. Names Lehman list, Popov Lego flip, Coast Runners, Christiano grasping, reward tampering.

nodes.title: The $47,000 Agent Loop: Why Token Budget Alerts Aren't Budget Enforcement
nodes.notes: Waxell incident writeup. Nov 2025: 4 LangChain A2A agents, Analyzer–Verifier ping-pong, 11 days / $47k. Named scholarly work: Palisade shutdown resistance. Observability tools (LangSmith/Helicone) skipped.

nodes.title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
nodes.notes: Patil et al. Cited by Relign as the source of the 'tool hallucination' framing. APIBench measures hallucinated / wrong API calls.

nodes.title: StableToolBench: Towards Stable Large-Scale Benchmarking on Tool Learning of Large Language Models
nodes.notes: Guo et al. Parent bench that Relign extends into RelyToolBench (missing-parameter and unmatched-tool subsets).

nodes.title: T-Eval: Evaluating the Tool Utilization Capability of Large Language Models Step by Step
nodes.notes: Chen et al. Step-level tool-utilization eval cited by Relign related work.

nodes.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
nodes.notes: Qin et al. ToolBench / ToolLLM; Relign reuses its pass-rate protocol then subtracts hallucination for RePR.

nodes.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
nodes.notes: Schick et al. Canonical self-supervised tool-use paper cited by Relign and IAL.

nodes.title: On Mitigating Code LLM Hallucinations with API Documentation
nodes.notes: Jain et al. Code-LLM hallucinated APIs mitigated with docs; closest Relign cite on content/format hallucination in code tools.

nodes.title: ToolBeHonest: A Multi-level Hallucination Diagnostic Benchmark for Tool-Augmented Large Language Models
nodes.notes: Zhang et al. EMNLP 2024. 700 samples / 7 tasks; depth (solvability, planning, missing-tool) × breadth (missing / potential / limited tools). GPT-4o 37.0/100.

nodes.title: ToolFuzz: Automated Agent Tool Testing
nodes.notes: Milev et al. Automated fuzzing of agent tools; cited by the agent-hallucination survey in the tool-stage section.

nodes.title: DebUnc: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Language Model Agent Communication with Uncertainty Estimations
nodes.notes: Yoffe et al. Uncertainty-aware mitigation of hallucinations in LLM agent-to-agent communication.

nodes.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
nodes.notes: Cemri et al. Survey cites MAST as the multi-agent failure/hallucination taxonomy.

nodes.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
nodes.notes: Yao et al. Canonical agent loop; cited by the hallucination survey and by IAL as the feedback-path primitive.

nodes.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
nodes.notes: Shinn et al. Verbal-RL agent loop cited by the survey and IAL as an unbounded retry pattern.

nodes.title: CrewAI issue #330: allow_delegation=True leading to infinite loop
nodes.notes: Named production IAL in IAL paper §I. Delegation flag creates an unbounded agent handoff.

nodes.title: LangGraph issue #6731: Agent infinite looping until recursion limit
nodes.notes: Named LangGraph IAL; bound is a recursion error, not a semantic stop. Same family as the $47k Analyzer–Verifier loop.

nodes.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
nodes.notes: Debenedetti et al. IAL cites AgentDojo as an agent security eval (injection can also induce non-termination). 97 tasks / 629 security cases.

nodes.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
nodes.notes: Zhang et al. ICLR 2025. IAL cites ASB as a security bench covering tool/memory/prompt stages. Peak ASR 84.3%.

nodes.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
nodes.notes: Wu et al. IAL analyzes AutoGen termination conditions as a framework-level bound that still admits IALs.

nodes.title: Agentproof: Static Verification of Agent Workflow Graphs
nodes.notes: Xavier et al. Static verification of agent workflow graphs; IAL related work on analysis of agent IR/graphs.

nodes.title: EvilGenie: A Reward Hacking Benchmark
nodes.notes: Gabor et al. Coding-agent reward-hacking bench; RHB related work. LLM-judge taxonomy of illegitimate test-passing.

nodes.title: School of Reward Hacks: Hacking Harmless Tasks Generalizes to Misaligned Behavior in LLMs
nodes.notes: Taylor et al. Training on harmless reward hacks generalizes to broader misalignment. Cited by RHB.

nodes.title: ImpossibleBench: Measuring LLMs' Propensity of Exploiting Test Cases
nodes.notes: Zhong, Raghunathan, Carlini. Propensity to exploit tests when the spec is impossible. Cited by RHB and EvilGenie.

nodes.title: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL
nodes.notes: MacDiarmid et al. Reward hacking in production RL produces broader misalignment. Cited by RHB.

nodes.title: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
nodes.notes: Turpin et al. Matches RHB finding that 72% of exploits have explicit CoT rationale.

nodes.title: Demonstrating Specification Gaming in Reasoning Models
nodes.notes: Palisade Research. Reasoning models hack the spec (e.g. chess). Cited by RHB as Research (2025).

nodes.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
nodes.notes: van der Weij et al. AgentMisalignment includes a cybersecurity sandbagging module and cites this paper.

nodes.title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
nodes.notes: Andriushchenko et al. AgentMisalignment related work: capability-to-harm vs propensity-to-misalign.

nodes.title: Large Language Models can Strategically Deceive their Users when Put Under Pressure
nodes.notes: Scheurer, Balesni, Hobbhahn. AgentMisalignment cites as prior spontaneous/strategic deception.

nodes.title: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
nodes.notes: Kinniment et al. (METR/ARC Evals). AgentMisalignment cites as realistic autonomous-task eval.

nodes.title: Breaking Agents: Compromising Autonomous LLM Agents Through Malfunction Amplification
nodes.notes: Zhang et al. AgentMisalignment cites as compromising autonomous agents via amplified malfunctions.

nodes.title: Deception in Reinforced Autonomous Agents
nodes.notes: Dogra et al. AgentMisalignment intro cite on deception in reinforced autonomous agents.

nodes.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
nodes.notes: Amodei et al. Langosco cites as the safety-problem catalog that goal-misgen instantiates empirically.

nodes.title: Risks from Learned Optimization in Advanced Machine Learning Systems
nodes.notes: Hubinger et al. Langosco treats goal-misgen as an empirical inner-alignment / mesa-objective failure.

nodes.title: Faulty Reward Functions in the Wild
nodes.notes: Clark & Amodei. Coast Runners boat loops on green blocks. Cited by Langosco and by the DeepMind spec-gaming blog.

nodes.title: The Effects of Reward Misspecification: Mapping and Mitigating Misaligned Models
nodes.notes: Pan, Bhatia, Steinhardt. Langosco cites as mapping how misspecified rewards produce misaligned policies.

nodes.title: Scalable Agent Alignment via Reward Modeling: a Research Direction
nodes.notes: Leike et al. Langosco cites scalable reward modeling as the intended-goal alternative to hard-coded rewards.

nodes.title: The Off-Switch Game
nodes.notes: Hadfield-Menell et al. Langosco cites the off-switch game as a corrigibility / shutdown-incentive prior.

nodes.title: The Surprising Creativity of Digital Evolution: A Collection of Anecdotes from the Evolutionary Computation and Artificial Life Research Communities
nodes.notes: Lehman et al. DeepMind blog's aggregated existing list of specification-gaming anecdotes.

nodes.title: Data-efficient Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dexterous Manipulation
nodes.notes: Popov et al. Named Lego stacking example: agent flips the red block to raise its bottom face instead of stacking.

nodes.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
nodes.notes: Christiano et al. Named grasping-task example: agent hovers between camera and object to fool the human evaluator.

nodes.title: Incomplete Tasks Induce Shutdown Resistance in Some Frontier LLMs
nodes.notes: Schlatter, Weinstein-Raun, Ladish (Palisade). Only scholarly work named by the $47k post: o3-class models sabotage shutdown even when told to allow it. Prompt-layer stop instructions are fragile.

nodes.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
nodes.notes: Greshake et al. AgentHarm cites as the canonical indirect-injection / LLM-app compromise paper.

nodes.title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
nodes.notes: Chen et al. AgentHarm cites memory/KB poisoning as an agent-specific attack.

nodes.title: Catastrophic Cyber Capabilities Benchmark (3CB): Robustly Evaluating LLM Agent Cyber Offense Capabilities
nodes.notes: Anurin et al. AgentHarm related work: agent cyber-offense capability bench.

nodes.title: Sycophancy to Subterfuge: Investigating Reward-Tampering in Large Language Models
nodes.notes: Denison et al. School of Reward Hacks cites this curriculum from sycophancy through subterfuge / reward tampering.

nodes.title: Recent frontier models are reward hacking
nodes.notes: METR blog. Cited by School of Reward Hacks and EvilGenie / RHB cluster.

nodes.title: Auditing Language Models for Hidden Objectives
nodes.notes: Marks et al. School of Reward Hacks cites hidden-objective auditing as the detection counterpart.

nodes.title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs could be an insider threat
nodes.notes: Lynch et al. / Anthropic. Palisade shutdown paper cites as related agentic-misalignment / insider-threat eval.

nodes.title: Safely Interruptible Agents
nodes.notes: Orseau & Armstrong UAI 2016. No arXiv; Palisade cites as the classical safe-interruptibility definition. MIRI announcement used as stable URL.

nodes.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
nodes.notes: Wallace et al. Palisade finds models obey allow-shutdown *less* when it is in the system prompt; cites instruction hierarchy.

nodes.title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
nodes.notes: Baker et al. EvilGenie cites monitoring of reasoning-model misbehavior and obfuscation risk.

nodes.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
nodes.notes: Jimenez et al. EvilGenie / RHB situate coding-agent hacks against SWE-bench-style issue solving.

nodes.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
nodes.notes: Hubinger et al. Denison cites sleeper/deceptive-alignment model organisms as the hidden-objective endpoint of reward tampering.

nodes.title: Reward Tampering Problems and Solutions in Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Influence Diagram Perspective
nodes.notes: Everitt et al. Denison cites the CID formulation of reward tampering (the formal paper behind the DeepMind tampering blog).
